activity.notes: Frederick Augustus III succeeded as Elector of Saxony in 1763. A regency administered Saxony during his minority, but his electoral reign remained continuous. On 20 December 1806 Saxony became a kingdom and he became King Frederick Augustus I. ATLAS therefore separates the Electorate of Saxony phase from the existing Kingdom of Saxony Activity.

sources.title: Frederick Augustus I and III, Elector and King of Saxony and Grand Duke of Warsaw — British Museum
sources.citation_text: The British Museum identifies Frederick Augustus as Elector of Saxony from 1763 to 1806, before he became King of Saxony.

sources.title: Wettiner — Deutsche Biographie
sources.citation_text: Deutsche Biographie identifies Friedrich August III, later King Friedrich August I, as ruling from 1763 and describes Saxony's elevation to a kingdom in 1806.
